questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in areas outside cities and villages with no posted speed limit?
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in areas outside cities and villages is 35 mph when no speed limit is posted.

questions.question: What should you do first when visibility is reduced?

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, slow down first. This is the most important step when road conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: What does NOT affect how far a vehicle takes to stop?

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road condition, and speed. The time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area your headlights show.
Use high beam headlights to see farther ahead.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slowly enough to stop within the area your headlights show.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Drive slowly enough that you can always stop within the distance your headlights illuminate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers about a curve to the right.

questions.question: How long can it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph to stop completely?
questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost 400 feet to stop at 55 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch carefully for traffic from other directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that another road crosses ahead.

questions.question: Children are playing near your driveway. What should you do before backing out?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children.
Honk your horn so children can hear you.
Walk behind your car to check the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your car to check the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Always get out and look behind your vehicle before backing up, especially when children are nearby. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, passing requires using the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass safely. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When should you start slowing down as you exit the interstate?

options.text: As you approach the deceleration lane.
When you enter the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you enter the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at your current speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When passing another car, when should you move back to the right lane?

options.text: When you are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only move back to the driving lane when you have enough space between you and the other vehicle. When you see both of that vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard or turn sharply in bad weather. These actions make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
At the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spots before changing lanes?

options.text: Use both the inside and outside rearview mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to check your blind spots before every lane change.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid yellow lines. The only exception is when you are making a turn.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Always drive at the speed limit.
Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Leave less space between you and the car ahead.
Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make sudden changes in speed or direction.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden changes in speed or direction on slippery roads. Slow down and do not use cruise control.

questions.question: If your car is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: A traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and continue through.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.
Speed up to get through before the light turns red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to pass through before the light turns red.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means you should stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about laws they must follow. These laws cover things like traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking. Regulatory signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols.

questions.question: What does a slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle. Vehicles with this emblem are driving 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When you merge onto the freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted freeway speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the speed of the traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at an intersection with this sign.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does your body process in one hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one alcoholic drink per hour on average. How impaired you become depends on many factors, including the amount you drink, how fast you drink it, your body weight, food intake, and your health.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right, and then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you.

questions.question: A green arrow turns into a solid green light. What can you do?

options.text: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
You may no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the arrow's direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. However, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic and know what to expect.
